https://www.dw.com/en/eco-wins-hungary-g.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5ISfP Yellow-bellied marmots are now officially internet famous Image: All Canada Photos/IMAGO Advertisement Hungary's former leader Viktor Orban called European Union climate policy a "utopian fantasy" and effectively banned wind turbines. And yet the country has quietly become Europe's solar leader , with 25% of its electricity now being being generated from the renewable energy source, ahead of sunnier countries like Spain, and Greece. The boom was driven not by climate concern but by self-sufficiency politics and cheap subsidies. Now a 450-megawatt park, just east of Budapest, is due online by September 2026. It's set to power around 106,000 households. Marmot researchers find a new way to fund their science When US federal funding dried up, researchers from UCLA and the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory got creative. They launched OnlyMarms: a free platform posting videos of yellow-bellied marmots eating, digging and scampering in the wild, where fans can donate to support the science. The team has tracked individually marked marmots in Colorado since 1962, building six decades of data on family lives, social behavior and responses to environmental change — and say studying marmot hibernation could even hold clues about human aging. Rome's 'big snake' gets a cooler future Corviale, a kilometer-long brutalist housing complex outside Rome nicknamed "the big snake," was completed in the 1980s and has since fallen into decay. With summers in some parts of Italy's now averaging around 30 degrees Celsius (86 Fahrenheit), life inside has become tough for its more than 4,000 residents. But upgrades are coming: a new library doubling as a cooling shelter, more trees and energy efficiency improvements, all aimed at helping Corviale stay cool as temperatures keep rising. Senegalese designer turns discarded textiles into sustainable fashion Berlin-based designer Mame Khady Badji transforms discarded clothing into bold garments inspired by her Senegalese heritage, combining traditional Ndiakhass techniques with contemporary streetwear. Her creations have drawn musicians, performers and creatives — and recently appeared at Berlin Fashion Week 2026. After moving to Germany in 2017, Badji built her label with support from Berlin's textile community. Now she's pursuing an ambitious goal: proving that recycled fashion can be both culturally rooted and commercially viable. Can sustainable fashion be profitable? Share this article paywall-free Email Copy Link The owner of a newly opened equipment sales and repair store on St. Michael’s Drive already has two other businesses to run, which might give some people pause about launching another venture. Not Sean Gabriel. “My dad taught me that work is everything,” said Gabriel, who also runs a commercial landscape company in Santa Fe and a 320-acre ranch in Prague, Okla., where he raises roping horses for professional rodeos. His father’s message was simple — work hard, and opportunities will present themselves. That’s what he’s trying to accomplish with his latest business, which is located at 720 St. Michael’s Drive, Suite P. New Mexico Power Equipment represents his first foray into the retail business. “I’m trying to work harder than anyone else,” he said. “I take a lot of pride in my work ethic.” The shop, which opened in mid-July, is located in a relatively small space — approximately 1,000 square feet, Gabriel said — but it specializes in Stihl equipment and repairs, with customer service a high priority. “I’m big on that — customer service and appreciation,” Gabriel said. Gabriel said he opened the shop because he saw a need for Stihl products and service in Santa Fe. “There’s long waits pretty much everywhere you go,” he said, something he hopes to remedy. Customer response has been good so far, Gabriel said. “The general consensus has been, it’s a breath of fresh air,” he said, noting his business already had earned seven five-star reviews on Google by last week. “Overall, it’s been a very positive experience.” Covering the bases Gabriel has a staff of four employees split evenly between the sales floor and the repairs department. The store carries a wide inventory of equipment designed for construction, manufacturing and agricultural purposes, including chainsaws, leaf blowers, hedgers, trimmers, lawn mowers, weed whackers and more. Although floor space may be limited, Gabriel said he makes a point of keeping his shelves filled. “I think we’re offering an inventory that’s more readily available,” he said, explaining he also keeps his storeroom well stocked with equipment that is in high demand. When a customer comes to the shop seeking a particular tool for a job, Gabriel said it’s his goal to avoid making them wait a couple of weeks for that equipment to be ordered and delivered. He said he understands that when contractors need equipment, they need it sooner rather than later. “I try to anticipate things,” he said. “I like to bend over backward for people and let them know they can depend on us.” New Mexico Power Equipment is located in the Plaza del Sol shopping center, a site Gabriel said he zeroed in on when the Smith’s Food and Drug location on Cerrillos Road closed its doors earlier this year, leaving the company’s store in Plaza del Sol as its only Santa Fe outlet. “I knew the Smith’s here was going to get much busier when that happened,” Gabriel said, adding many of his customers have found his business after shopping at the adjacent grocery store. “The plaza has filled up. It’s an excellent location. It has great parking and good visibility, so to me, it was a no-brainer.” Gabriel, a Santa Fe native who moved to Canada in his early teens and spent time in California and Arizona before returning to New Mexico in his late 20s, said he’s used to launching and running businesses. He’s always had an entrepreneurial streak — another trait he picked up from his father. “I’ve been self-employed since I was about 23,” he said. New Mexico Power Equipment is only open on weekdays for now, but Gabriel said he hopes to expand its hours to Saturdays by the end of summer. “I love business, and I love building successful businesses,” he said. “So I know what successful customer service is. I know what people want and expect. It’s challenging to achieve successful customer service, and that’s our primary goal. That’s what we do, and we will accomplish that.” Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save If You Go What: New Mexico Power Equipment Where: 720 St. Michael’s Drive, Suite P Hours: 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. weekdays More information: 505-479-7080 or newmexico power.com Takeaways New Mexico Power Equipment opened in the middle of July in the Plaza del Sol shopping center on St. Michael’s Drive. Owner Sean Gabriel also owns a commercial landscape company and a horse ranch. Beállítom A Mi Hazánk Radetzky Andrást jelöli a Médiatanácsba Tóth Máté helyére – jelentette be kedden Apáti István, a párt országgyűlési képviselője. Tóth Máté azután mondott le a Médiatanácsban elfoglalt posztjáról , hogy múlt hétvégén a Mi Hazánk egyik alelnökévé választották. A két tisztség azonban összeférhetetlen egymással a médiatörvény rendelkezései szerint, ezért Tóthnak választania kellett, hogy melyikről mond le. Ő pedig úgy döntött, hogy a Médiatanácsból távozik. Egy keddi sajtótájékoztatón Apáti István, a Mi Hazánk alelnöke azt mondta, pártjuk mihamarabb kezdeményezi új jelölési eljárás indítását, és Radetzky András rádiós szakembert, a Pázmány Péter Katolikus Egyetem oktatóját, docensét, a Magyar Katolikus Rádió Zrt. vezérigazgató-helyettesét kívánják delegálni a Médiatanácsba. Radetzky a sajtótájékoztatón azt mondta: a nap folyamán kezdeményezte távozását a Magyar Katolikus Rádió Zrt.-nél. Elmondta, hatalmas megtiszteltetésnek és kihívásnak tekinti hogy részt vehet „a magyar médiarendszer gyógyulásának folyamatában”. Radetzky arról is beszélt, hogy az elmúlt évek számos diszfunkciót hoztak felszínre, elsősorban a jogalkalmazás területén fennálló hiányosságok, hibák képében. Tóth Mátét éppen egy hete választotta a Médiatanács tagjává az Országgyűlés, miközben a Fidesz és a KDNP jelöltjét a tiszás képviselők többsége nem támogatta .
